findings.title: 3.7 commit gate cannot pass; adoptionBuild.integration.test.ts is deleted only at 4.1
findings.description: Task 3.3 makes `createContextPipeline` take one parameter. Task 3.7 then requires `pnpm -r test` and `pnpm typecheck` to pass before committing 3.3–3.6. But no task in 3.x touches `adoptionBuild.integration.test.ts`, and it is deleted only at 4.1 (task lines 144, 148). Line 68 calls `createContextPipeline(dir, { adoptionStateWrites, squadronProbe: fakeProbe })`. After 3.3 that is a type error if tests are in the typecheck, and its brownfield cases (3–6, 8, 9, 11–13) assert the prompt swap, Adoption Facts, state writes or `AdoptionError`. Those behaviors are gone at 3.3, so those cases will fail at 3.7. Fix: add deleting this file to 3.3. It has no dependents in 3.x.

findings.title: The services-import grep in 3.3 fails on a comment the task does not mention
findings.description: Line 9 is a comment: "contracts.ts only (never adoption/index.ts)". The 3.3 success check (task line 109), `grep -rn "adoption/\|detection/" packages/core/src/services`, matches it, so the check prints a line even when every import is gone. Task 3.3 says only to remove imports. Add: delete the comment on line 9, since it describes a boundary that no longer exists.

findings.title: Commit points are checkbox items, not `**Commit**:` markers
findings.description: The commits are written as `- [ ] **2.3 Commit** …` and `- [ ] Commit: …` at lines 79, 99–101, 134, 148, 155, 163, 169, 186 and 206. The convention is plain `**Commit**:` lines at working, tested points, never checkboxes. A checkbox commit also conflicts with the required order (implement, task-checker, then commit): the box cannot be checked before the commit that contains it. Convert each to a plain line after its section's last verified step. The resulting cadence (2.3, 3.2a, 3.7, 4.1–4.4, 5.1, plus 6.3 if needed) is reasonable.

findings.title: The build-order note in section 3 is wrong, and the 4.x gates may read a stale dist
findings.description: Line 87 says only mcp-server typecheck fails between 3.4 and 3.6. That is not true. `packages/cli/src/commands/build.ts:84` still passes a second argument, so cli fails from the 3.4 build until 3.5, and mcp-server (`contextTools.ts:100`) fails until 3.6. Correct the note. Also, cli and mcp-server typecheck against core's `dist/`, but the task rebuilds core only at 3.4. Sections 4.1–4.4 change core exports, so their `pnpm typecheck` gates may check against a stale build. Either state that the root typecheck builds core first (I did not verify this) or add `pnpm --filter @context-forge/core build` to each 4.x gate.

findings.title: The purity test covers two adoption.state values, but the criterion says "whatever it holds"
findings.description: The design criterion (design line 189) is that a Phase 0 brownfield build returns the concept prompt and writes nothing, "whatever adoption.state holds". Task 5.1 runs the CLI with no toml and with `in_progress`, and MCP with `in_progress`. `complete` and `declined` are never run, though the build reads neither. The full value set is `ADOPTION_STATES` in `packages/core/src/config/ConfigKeys.ts:28`. Have the CLI path iterate over that constant, not a literal list.

findings.title: The mutation check in 5.1 is not required by any criterion
findings.description: Adding a temporary `writeFileSync` to the test, confirming failure and reverting is a hand edit to a test file, and it can be left in place. No success criterion or design decision (D5) asks for it. Keep it as an explicit one-off manual check with a named revert, or drop it.

findings.title: Paths mix `packages/core/…` and `core/…`
findings.description: Most items use `core/src/…` and `cli/…`. Items 2.1, 6.1 and 6.2 use `packages/…`. The real paths are under `packages/`. Say once at the top that paths are relative to `packages/`, or use full paths throughout.

findings.title: Task 1.1 does not check for an unregistered worktree
findings.description: This checkout is a git worktree (`…/wt/context-forge-268-tasks`). The project rules require `cf worktree list --json` to show the checkout as registered, and stop-and-ask otherwise. Task 1.1 checks only that `pwd` is "the repo root", which means something different inside a worktree. Add the registration check as a sub-bullet.

findings.title: Later-phase golden coverage is one case
findings.description: The criterion says "greenfield, already-planned and later-phase builds are byte-identical" (design line 190). The golden set is greenfield at Phase 0 and planned at Phase 4, which follows D6. That is probably enough: the removed code renders output only when the adoption fields are set (`SectionBuilder.ts:160`, `ContextTemplateEngine.ts:113`), and those are set only on brownfield Phase 0 builds. If the PM wants more, add a second later phase. Otherwise, note in the golden test why one phase suffices.

findings.title: The 6.2 export audit has no mechanical check
findings.description: "For each symbol still exported … confirm there is a production consumer" is a judgment step with no command. Suggest listing the export names in `packages/core/src/adoption/index.ts` and `packages/core/src/detection/index.ts`, grepping each name outside its own module, and comparing the result to the design's Interfaces Required list.

findings.title: The 6.3 walkthrough omits the scratch-repo preconditions
findings.description: Step 1 of the design requires a repo with more than 2000 source lines, no `project-documents/user/architecture` artifacts, `cf init`, and Phase 0. Task 6.3 says only "a scratch brownfield repo under /tmp". The reference to the design is enough to find these, but list them here, because they are what make the check mean something.

findings.title: Coverage and sequencing otherwise hold
findings.description:
- Every `createContextPipeline` caller is assigned, except `adoptionBuild.integration.test.ts` (see the FAIL). Callers are `build.ts` and `contextTools.ts`, `build.integration.test.ts`, `CoreServiceFactory.test.ts`, `pipeline-integration.test.ts`, and `adoptionParity.test.ts`.
- The probe is deleted (4.4) after its last production consumer is removed (3.3), and after the contracts import is removed (4.2).
- The 4.4 probe-name grep, run case-insensitively, is clean once the listed tasks run. The 6.2 removed-name grep leaves only the expected `COMPREHENSION_PROFILE_VARIABLE` exception (`comprehensionAnalysis.ts:15`).
- 5.1 reads the deleted parity helper from the target with `git show`, so it does not depend on 3.6 being in the working tree.
- The guide-warning tests named in 6.1 exist (`cli/tests/commands/build.test.ts:91`, `mcp-server/tests/contextTools.test.ts:162`). Sections 3.5 and 3.6 keep their assertions.
- The slice restates no NFR, so no load test or CI gate is needed.
- Scope: nothing beyond the design, apart from the 5.1 mutation step (NOTE above). The final full gate runs at both 3.7 and 6.1. The design asks for the final pass, so this is cost, not a gap.
